about.title: Petaluma Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Petaluma's mix of historic downtown storefronts, shopping centers along E Washington Street, and residential complexes near N Mcdowell Boulevard means uneven walkways, wet floors, and poorly lit stairwells are common causes of falls. Sonoma County property owners have a legal duty to keep premises reasonably safe, but proving a claim means showing they knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why acting quickly matters — surveillance footage from a grocery store or apartment lobby often gets erased within days or weeks. If you were hurt in a fall anywhere in Petaluma, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who understands how to gather that evidence and evaluate whether the property owner may be responsible. There's no obligation, and no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Connect With an Attorney Through LawProactive

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify prior complaints, maintenance logs, or inspection records that support this.

items.title: Video Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Petaluma businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days. An attorney can send preservation requests quickly so this evidence isn't lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Affects Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced but not eliminated even if you were partly at fault. An attorney can help frame the facts fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Petaluma?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim against a private property owner. If a government entity owns the property — such as a City of Petaluma sidewalk — the deadline is much shorter, often just six months. It's best to get evaluated as soon as possible so deadlines aren't missed.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for my fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were somewhat careless, you may still recover a portion of damages reduced by your share of fault. This is a fact-specific determination an attorney can help assess.

items.question: Does it matter that my fall happened near a busy Petaluma corridor like N Mcdowell Boulevard?
items.answer: Location itself doesn't determine fault, but nearby traffic, foot patterns, or public-record collision counts can sometimes be relevant context for how a property was maintained or used. An attorney can review the specific circumstances of where and how you fell.
